findings.title: Planning requires ActionPackage formation but does not plan a Core package-preparation seam
findings.observation: The approved Explore asks how Core freezes existing exact current Action/Run/role/authority/predecessor facts into an ActionPackage, the Delivery goal says Core prepares an exact ActionPackage, and the Spec requires the system to form a closed ActionPackage. However Task 1.1 only adds an ActionPackage type/validator and tests that manually supplied prepared/resumed packages are accepted; Design likewise does not identify a concrete package-formation operation. The current task list can therefore be completed without Core gaining any operation that actually constructs the package handed to an external executor.
findings.impact: Apply could produce a validator/admission library while leaving the prepare half of the ActionPackage boundary absent. A later execution host would still have to invent package construction semantics, risking drift in run/action/state/role/authority/predecessor linkage and recreating the old prepare-to-executor integration gap at the domain boundary.
findings.requiredRevision: Add the smallest pure package-preparation/formation seam to Design and Tasks, and tighten the package contract as needed so it emits the closed canonical ActionPackage from already-validated current facts. Reusing RunContextRecord plus exact CurrentAction, or an equivalent minimal canonical input, is sufficient. Verify prepared/resumed formation and fail-closed terminal/mismatched inputs. Do not add persistence I/O, Policy, transport, Agent invocation, new package identity, replay infrastructure, or terminal orchestration.

applyReadiness.statement: The Proposal is scoped and otherwise coherent, but Apply readiness requires an explicit plan for Core to construct the ActionPackage that the Spec says it can form; type validation alone does not satisfy the prepare half of this Change.

limitations: This finding does not require provider transport, external Agent invocation, repository synchronization, Policy, resume/terminal/STOP orchestration, or CLI integration in this Change.
